title: The harvester
summary: The Harvester is a novel by Gene Stratton-Porter, first published in 1911, about David Langston, a man who gathers medicinal herbs, roots and barks from the woods around Loon Lake near the small town of Onabasha. Living a self-sufficient life in the forests inherited from his mother, he is a carver of wooden candlesticks and a naturalist who has long avoided the city and romance. The story follows his reluctant move into the world of commerce and medicine, and his encounters with a hospital setting, doctors and nurses, and an unhappy young woman, Ruth Jameson, who arrives in his life in crisis. Their relationship develops against a backdrop of rural nature, family grief, and questions about love, duty and self-worth. The book also contrasts the simple, honest life of the woods with the restless, often shallow life of the city, a theme the author develops through a large cast of characters including doctors, traders, lawyers and a gentle older neighbour. The excerpt suggests a romantic, lyrical tone, with extensive attention to birds, plants, seasons and the moral character of its hero.
